jess: heads-up — production p99 spiked by ~600ms around 14:03 UTC after yesterday's runtime change. p95 mostly unchanged.
max: confirmed on canary. repro with loadgen at 2k concurrent connections: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~980ms when microbatch=8. when microbatch=4 p95 ~260ms, p99 ~420ms.
srini: interesting — kernel selector started preferring 'fused-attn-v2' for >128 seq lengths in that deploy. suspecting cache interaction + larger mb sizing.
jess: timeline: deploy 1729450000 swapped kernel heuristic + bumped default microbatch target from 4->8. Ops around the same time had spike in cache evictions.
olivia: quick profiling results from today's run (short):
```
rpc_latencies: {mean: 120ms, p95: 230ms, p99: 980ms}
kv_cache: hit_rate: 81%, evictions/sec: 120 -> jump to 520 during peak
microbatch: size_dist: {4:10%,8:70%,16:20%}
cpu: kernel-switch overhead visible when concurrent kv miss + kernel load
```
max: reproducer notes: If I force kernel to 'baseline-attn' and microbatch=8, p99 drops to ~420ms but throughput drops ~8%. If I keep fused-attn and microbatch=4, throughput drops ~15% but p99 is acceptable.
srini: so it's a tradeoff: fused-attn gives throughput at scale but is more sensitive to cache churn/eviction stalls, which amplify tail. baseline-attn is more resilient.
jess: logs show eviction stalls creating 10-30ms pauses that stack with kernel activation costs. under high concurrency those stack to hundreds.
olivia: perf-bot captured stack traces during one tail spike — most time in kernel init + kv fetch path.
perf-bot: <attached profile link> https://perf.internal/runs/1729456
max: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) lower default microbatch target back to 4 for prod tier B; 2) increase KV cache capacity for hot-shards; 3) add small hysteresis to kernel selector to avoid switching on transient seq-length distribution changes.
srini: also consider increasing kV eviction hysteresis: only evict if pressure sustained >10s or eviction rate >300/sec. reduces oscillation.
jess: canary plan: revert microbatch default to 4 and enable kernel selector hysteresis; scale one pool's KV cache + run 1-hour soak at 2.5k concurrent.
olivia: I'll queue canary. deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/runtime-revert-1729457200 -> starting 1729457200 UTC :rocket:
max: I'll instrument additional p99 probes and a tail trace sampler. If that knocks down tail without >10% throughput loss we can keep fused-attn with tuning.
srini: for longer term: add kernel warmup path that preloads fused kernels on instance start to reduce init spikes, and explore async kv fetch so kernel waits less on cache misses.
jess: agreed. documenting perf regression as: "tail-latency amplification due to kernel selection + increased microbatch sizing under KV eviction pressure". filing a postmortem if canary doesn't resolve.
olivia: thanks — kicking off canary now, will report back in thread. :thumbsup:
